wins.claim: KerfDesk ships a full pre-run simulator (scrub, play/pause, speeds, pass stepper, external .nc playback) where LaserGRBL documents no simulation playback at all.
gSender's visualizer animates only the live job, so KerfDesk's scrubber/speed/step preview simulator has no counterpart there.
KerfDesk's preview is parity-tested against the emitted job and perceptually mask-verified, while Carbide Create's community reports blank simulation pages and unrendered small pockets.
A scrub-coupled removal grid with perceptually verified V-carve depth math and .nc re-import parity edges Carbide Create's defect-prone animated sim.
KerfDesk simulates step-through material removal coupled to the scrubber, while Easel's Simulate playback animates path lines only with a static 3D result render.

gaps.claim: No vector shade-by-power at all - drawCut ignores layer color so 10% and 90% power look identical, an un-ADR'd divergence from the LightBurn baseline ADR-028 itself records (5.6 severity bump).
Playback is distance-compressed over fixed 60/30/10s wall durations instead of LightBurn's 1/10x-40x actual-speed animation with Start-Here resume; no per-command step-through.

The physics estimator has never been validated against a real machine and carries three open defects (bidirectional ignored, placement ignored, no elapsed/remaining) vs LightBurn's controller-synced estimates.
KerfDesk's 2.5D flat-rect heightfield with no textures, undercuts, or visual inspection trails VCarve's textured, animated, both-sides simulation ceiling.
No user-facing performance modes and zero production-scale measurement vs gSender's documented three-preset Lightweight Mode built for large files.
KerfDesk's perceptual proof covers only 32px synthetic fill/cross-hatch cases while LightBurn's preview is community-trusted ground truth at production scale.
